course: ACT Math - Number, Algebra, Functions, Geometry and Data
attribution: Original scope and sequence authored for the Luminfest Learning Harness, dedicated to the public domain under CC0.
scope: Structure only: concept titles, unit order and prerequisite intent. No third-party curriculum text is reproduced, and no restricted source is ingested.
description: A complete ACT Mathematics course: rational and irrational numbers, exponent properties, vectors, matrices and complex numbers, linear, quadratic, polynomial, rational and radical algebra with systems and inequalities, functions and their transformations, sequences, trigonometry, exponential and logarithmic functions, geometry from transformations and similarity through coordinate geometry, conics and circles, univariate and bivariate statistics with inference and probability, the integrating essential skills the test assumes, and modelling as a practice rather than a topic.

concepts.title: Rational Numbers as Ratios
concepts.summary: A number is rational exactly when it equals a ratio of two integers, and its decimal expansion then terminates or repeats a fixed block.

concepts.title: Recognising Irrational Numbers
concepts.summary: A number is irrational when no ratio of integers equals it, so its decimal neither terminates nor repeats, as with the square root of 2.

concepts.title: Density and Ordering on the Number Line
concepts.summary: Between any two distinct real numbers lies both a rational and an irrational number, so there is no smallest positive real number.

concepts.title: Product and Quotient Rules
concepts.summary: For a nonzero base a, a^m times a^n is a^(m+n) and a^m divided by a^n is a^(m-n), because multiplying counts factors and dividing cancels them.

concepts.title: Zero, Negative, and Fractional Exponents
concepts.summary: For nonzero a, a^0 is 1 and a^(-n) is 1/a^n, while a^(m/n) is the nth root of a^m whenever that root is a real number.

concepts.title: Power of a Product and Power of a Power
concepts.summary: (ab)^n equals a^n b^n and (a^m)^n equals a^(mn), but (a+b)^n is not a^n + b^n because an exponent does not distribute over a sum.

concepts.title: Vector Components and Magnitude
concepts.summary: A plane vector is an ordered pair of components, and its magnitude is the square root of the sum of their squares, which is a distance in the plane.

concepts.title: Vector Addition and Scalar Multiplication
concepts.summary: Vectors add component by component and scale by multiplying each component, so a negative scalar reverses direction without changing the line of action.

concepts.title: Matrix Dimensions and Products
concepts.summary: A product AB exists only when the column count of A equals the row count of B, and matrix multiplication is not commutative in general.

concepts.title: The Imaginary Unit
concepts.summary: The imaginary unit i satisfies i^2 = -1, which makes x^2 + 1 = 0 solvable and gives every negative real number two square roots.

concepts.title: Arithmetic with Complex Numbers
concepts.summary: Complex numbers add part by part and multiply by distributing with i^2 = -1, so the sum and product of complex numbers stay complex.

concepts.title: The Complex Conjugate
concepts.summary: Multiplying a + bi by its conjugate a - bi gives the real number a^2 + b^2, which is how a complex denominator is cleared.

concepts.title: Units as Part of the Quantity
concepts.summary: A measurement is a number together with a unit, so an answer that lacks the unit the question asked for has not answered the question.

concepts.title: Dimensional Analysis
concepts.summary: Multiplying by a conversion factor equal to one changes the unit without changing the value, and the unwanted units must cancel completely.
prerequisites: Units as Part of the Quantity

concepts.title: Precision and Significant Figures
concepts.summary: A computed result carries no more precision than its least precise input, so a calculator display is rounded to that precision rather than quoted whole.

concepts.title: Solving Linear Equations
concepts.summary: A linear equation is solved by applying the same operation to both sides until the variable stands alone, which preserves the solution set at every step.

concepts.title: Reversing an Inequality
concepts.summary: Multiplying or dividing both sides of an inequality by a negative number reverses the symbol, because that operation reflects the number line.

concepts.title: Solving a Formula for a Variable
concepts.summary: Rearranging a formula for a named variable treats every other variable as a constant, so the inverse operations are applied in reverse order.

concepts.title: Factoring and the Zero Product Property
concepts.summary: If a product equals zero then at least one factor equals zero, so a factored quadratic equation splits into two linear equations.

concepts.title: The Quadratic Formula and Discriminant
concepts.summary: For ax^2 + bx + c = 0 with a not zero, x = (-b +/- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac))/(2a), and the sign of b^2 - 4ac gives two, one, or no real solutions.
prerequisites: Factoring and the Zero Product Property

concepts.title: Sign Analysis of a Quadratic Inequality
concepts.summary: A quadratic inequality is solved from its zeros and the sign of the leading coefficient: an upward parabola is positive outside its roots and negative between them.

topics.topic: Rational and Radical Expressions and Equations

concepts.title: Restricted Domains of Rational Expressions
concepts.summary: A rational expression is undefined where its denominator is zero, so those values are excluded before a common factor is cancelled.

concepts.title: Common Denominators for Rational Expressions
concepts.summary: Rational expressions are added by rewriting each over a common denominator, and multiplying numerator and denominator by the same nonzero factor changes nothing.

concepts.title: Extraneous Solutions from Squaring
concepts.summary: A radical equation can produce extraneous solutions because squaring both sides is not reversible, so every candidate is checked in the original equation.

concepts.title: Degree, Zeros, and End Behaviour
concepts.summary: A polynomial of degree n has at most n real zeros and at most n - 1 turning points, and its end behaviour follows the sign of its leading coefficient.

concepts.title: Remainder and Factor Theorems
concepts.summary: Dividing p(x) by x - c leaves remainder p(c), so c is a zero of p exactly when x - c is a factor of p.

concepts.title: Multiplying and Dividing Polynomials
concepts.summary: Every term of one polynomial multiplies every term of the other, and division by a monomial distributes over the terms while division by a binomial needs long division.

concepts.title: Substitution and Elimination
concepts.summary: Substitution or elimination reduces a system of two linear equations to one equation in one variable, and the second variable follows by back substitution.

concepts.title: The Three Solution Cases
concepts.summary: Two lines in a plane meet once, never, or at every point, so a linear system has exactly one solution, none, or infinitely many.

concepts.title: Half-Planes from Two-Variable Inequalities
concepts.summary: The solution set of a linear inequality in two variables is a half-plane, and one test point decides which side of the boundary satisfies it.

concepts.title: Equivalent Forms of One Relationship
concepts.summary: Factored, standard, and vertex forms describe the same quadratic, so the form is chosen for what it displays: zeros, y-intercept, or turning point.

concepts.title: Interpreting Parameters in Context
concepts.summary: In y = mx + b the slope is the change per input unit and b is the starting value, and each parameter carries the units of the quantity it describes.

concepts.title: Agreement of Equation, Table, and Graph
concepts.summary: An equation, its table, and its graph describe the same relationship, so a disagreement between any two of them exposes an algebra or scale error.

concepts.title: Function Definition and Vertical Line Test
concepts.summary: A function assigns exactly one output to each input, so a graph is a function exactly when no vertical line meets it more than once.

concepts.title: Domain and Range
concepts.summary: The domain is the set of inputs the rule accepts, limited by division by zero and even roots of negatives, and the range is the set of outputs actually produced.
prerequisites: Function Definition and Vertical Line Test

concepts.title: Average Rate of Change
concepts.summary: The average rate of change between two inputs is the change in output divided by the change in input, which is the slope of the secant line.

concepts.title: Composition of Functions
concepts.summary: The composition f(g(x)) applies g first and f second, so its domain excludes inputs that g rejects and inputs whose g(x) f cannot evaluate.

concepts.title: Transformations of Graphs
concepts.summary: Adding a constant to the output shifts a graph vertically, adding inside the input shifts it horizontally in the opposite direction, and a factor stretches or reflects it.

concepts.title: Inverse Functions
concepts.summary: An inverse swaps the roles of input and output and undoes the original, and it is a function only where the original is one-to-one.

concepts.title: Arithmetic Sequences and Their Sums
concepts.summary: An arithmetic sequence adds a constant difference, so a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d and the first n terms sum to n(a_1 + a_n)/2.

concepts.title: Geometric Sequences and Their Sums
concepts.summary: A geometric sequence multiplies by a constant ratio, so a_n = a_1 r^(n-1) and a finite sum is a_1(1 - r^n)/(1 - r) when r is not 1.

concepts.title: Recursive versus Explicit Rules
concepts.summary: A recursive rule needs a starting term and the previous term, while an explicit rule gives any term from its position alone, which is what makes a distant term computable.

concepts.title: Right-Triangle Ratios
concepts.summary: In a right triangle sine, cosine, and tangent are fixed ratios of two sides, so one acute angle and one side determine the remaining sides.

concepts.title: Unit Circle and Radian Measure
concepts.summary: On the unit circle the cosine and sine of an angle are the coordinates of the point it reaches, and pi radians equal 180 degrees.

concepts.title: Period, Amplitude, and Midline
concepts.summary: For y = A sin(Bx + C) + D the amplitude is |A|, the period is 2pi/|B|, and the midline is y = D, so each parameter changes one visible feature.

concepts.title: Exponential Growth and Decay
concepts.summary: In f(x) = a b^x the base b is the factor per unit step, so b > 1 grows, 0 < b < 1 decays, and the percent change per step is b - 1.

concepts.title: Logarithms as Inverses
concepts.summary: log_b x is the exponent that turns b into x, so it inverts b^x and accepts only positive inputs because no power of b is zero or negative.

concepts.title: Solving Exponential and Logarithmic Equations
concepts.summary: An exponential equation yields to a logarithm of both sides and a logarithmic equation to rewriting it in exponential form, with every candidate checked against the domain.

concepts.title: Rigid Motions Preserve Congruence
concepts.summary: Translations, rotations, and reflections preserve every length and angle, so a figure and its image under a rigid motion are congruent.

concepts.title: Dilations and Scale Factor
concepts.summary: A dilation multiplies every length by its scale factor and preserves angle measures, so it changes size while keeping the shape.

concepts.title: Deductive Reasoning and Counterexamples
concepts.summary: A proof derives each statement from givens and established results, and a single counterexample is enough to refute a universal claim.

concepts.title: Similar Triangles and Proportional Sides
concepts.summary: Two triangles are similar when two pairs of corresponding angles agree, and then every pair of corresponding sides shares one ratio.

concepts.title: Pythagorean Theorem and Its Converse
concepts.summary: In a right triangle the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the legs, and the converse guarantees a triangle satisfying it is right.

concepts.title: Law of Sines and Law of Cosines
concepts.summary: The law of sines relates each side to the sine of its opposite angle, and the law of cosines extends the Pythagorean theorem to triangles without a right angle.

concepts.title: Distance and Midpoint
concepts.summary: The distance between two points is the hypotenuse of a right triangle whose legs are the coordinate differences, and the midpoint averages the coordinates.

concepts.title: Slope Criteria for Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
concepts.summary: Two nonvertical lines are parallel exactly when their slopes are equal and perpendicular exactly when their slopes have product -1.

concepts.title: Equations of Circles in the Plane
concepts.summary: A circle with centre (h, k) and radius r satisfies (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2, and completing the square recovers the centre and radius from a general equation.
prerequisites: Slope Criteria for Parallel and Perpendicular Lines

concepts.title: Standard Forms of the Conics
concepts.summary: Each conic has a standard form whose parameters display its centre or vertex, its axis, and its size, so a shape is identified from its equation.

concepts.title: Completing the Square to Classify
concepts.summary: Completing the square in x and y turns a general second-degree equation into standard form, which shows which conic it is and whether it is degenerate.

concepts.title: Foci and Eccentricity
concepts.summary: An ellipse is the set of points whose distances to two foci have a constant sum, and its eccentricity measures how far it departs from a circle.

concepts.title: Central Angles and Arcs
concepts.summary: A central angle has the same measure as its intercepted arc, so an arc length is that fraction of the circumference.

concepts.title: Inscribed Angles
concepts.summary: An inscribed angle measures half of its intercepted arc, which is why an angle inscribed in a semicircle is a right angle.

concepts.title: Chords, Tangents, and Secants
concepts.summary: A tangent line is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, and a radius that bisects a chord is perpendicular to that chord.

concepts.title: Perimeter, Circumference, and Area
concepts.summary: Area scales as the square of a length scale factor, so doubling every dimension of a figure multiplies its area by four.

concepts.title: Surface Area and Volume
concepts.summary: Volume scales as the cube of a length scale factor while surface area scales as its square, so doubling a solid multiplies volume by eight and surface area by four.

concepts.title: Density and Geometric Modelling
concepts.summary: A geometric model answers a real question only when the units agree: volume times density gives mass, and area times a coverage rate gives a total amount.

concepts.title: Measures of Center
concepts.summary: The mean is pulled toward a skew or an outlier while the median is not, so the median better describes a typical value in a skewed distribution.

concepts.title: Measures of Spread
concepts.summary: Range, interquartile range, and standard deviation all measure spread, and the interquartile range resists outliers as the median does.

concepts.title: Shape from Displays
concepts.summary: A histogram or box plot shows shape, centre, spread, and outliers together, and no single summary statistic can reveal a second peak.

concepts.title: Scatterplots and Association
concepts.summary: A scatterplot displays the direction, form, and strength of an association between two quantitative variables, which a correlation alone cannot show.

concepts.title: The Least-Squares Regression Line
concepts.summary: The least-squares line minimises the sum of squared residuals, so it balances prediction errors rather than passing through the most data points.

concepts.title: Correlation and Prediction
concepts.summary: The correlation coefficient measures only the strength and direction of a linear association, so a strong correlation never by itself establishes causation.

concepts.title: Samples and Populations
concepts.summary: A statistic computed from a random sample estimates a population parameter, and the sampling method decides whether that estimate can be trusted.

concepts.title: The Central Limit Theorem
concepts.summary: For a large random sample the sample mean is approximately normal with mean mu and standard deviation sigma over the square root of n, whatever the population shape.

concepts.title: Null Hypotheses and p-Values
concepts.summary: A hypothesis test compares the observed statistic with what the null hypothesis predicts, and a small p-value means the observation is unlikely under that null.

concepts.title: Probability as a Long-Run Proportion
concepts.summary: A probability lies between 0 and 1 and equals the proportion of trials in which the event occurs as the number of trials grows without bound.

concepts.title: Addition Rule and Mutually Exclusive Events
concepts.summary: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B), and the subtracted term vanishes only when A and B cannot occur together.

concepts.title: Conditional Probability and Independence
concepts.summary: P(A given B) = P(A and B)/P(B), and A and B are independent exactly when that conditional probability equals P(A).
prerequisites: Addition Rule and Mutually Exclusive Events

concepts.title: The Multiplication Principle
concepts.summary: If one stage can be done in m ways and the next in n ways, the two stages together can be done in mn ways, which multiplies through any number of stages.

concepts.title: Permutations Count Ordered Arrangements
concepts.summary: The number of ordered arrangements of r items chosen from n distinct items is n!/(n - r)!, because a different order is a different arrangement.

concepts.title: Combinations Count Unordered Selections
concepts.summary: The number of unordered selections of r items from n is n!/(r!(n - r)!), which is the permutation count divided by the r! orders of one set.

concepts.title: Field Properties of Real Numbers
concepts.summary: Real numbers are closed under addition and multiplication, both operations commute and associate, and multiplication distributes over addition, which is what licenses every rearrangement.

topics.topic: Computation and Problem Solving with Real Numbers

concepts.title: Signed Arithmetic and Order of Operations
concepts.summary: Grouping and exponents are evaluated first, then multiplication and division left to right, then addition and subtraction, with sign rules applied at each step.

concepts.title: Setting Up and Solving a Proportion
concepts.summary: A proportion states two equal ratios, and cross multiplication clears the denominators, which is the same step as multiplying both sides by their product.

concepts.title: Translating Words into Symbols
concepts.summary: Each operation word maps to one symbol and order words such as twice the sum fix the grouping, so a phrase is translated one operation at a time.

topics.topic: Writing and Solving Simple Equations and Inequalities

concepts.title: Isolating the Unknown
concepts.summary: An equation or inequality is solved by undoing operations in reverse order on both sides, and multiplying or dividing by a negative reverses an inequality.

concepts.title: Conversion Factors in One Step
concepts.summary: A conversion factor is a ratio of two equal quantities, so multiplying by it changes only the unit and the unit being replaced must cancel.

topics.topic: Properties of Lines, Angles, and Shapes

concepts.title: Angle Relationships in Figures
concepts.summary: Vertical angles are equal, angles on a straight line sum to 180 degrees, and the angles of a triangle sum to 180 degrees, which fixes a missing angle.

concepts.title: Area of Composite Figures
concepts.summary: A composite figure is measured by adding or subtracting the areas of the shapes it decomposes into, with every length first converted to one unit.

concepts.title: Volume and Surface Area Formulas
concepts.summary: A prism or cylinder has volume equal to base area times height, a pyramid or cone has one third of that, and surface area sums the exposed faces.

concepts.title: Slope, Midpoint, and Distance from Coordinates
concepts.summary: Between two points the slope is the ratio of the coordinate differences, the midpoint averages the coordinates, and the distance is the hypotenuse of those differences.

concepts.title: Right Triangles and the Distance Formula
concepts.summary: In a right triangle the hypotenuse squared equals the sum of the legs squared, and the coordinate distance formula is that theorem applied to the two coordinate differences.

concepts.title: Reading a Scatterplot
concepts.summary: A scatterplot is read for direction, strength, and form of association, and a point far off the pattern is an outlier that can dominate a fitted line.

concepts.title: Choosing a Summary Statistic
concepts.summary: The mean and standard deviation describe symmetric data, while the median and interquartile range describe skewed data or data carrying outliers.

concepts.title: Inference from a Sample
concepts.summary: A conclusion about a population drawn from a sample is only as sound as the sample is random, so a biased sample supports no inference however large it is.

concepts.title: Probability from Equally Likely Outcomes
concepts.summary: When outcomes are equally likely the probability of an event is the number of favourable outcomes divided by the total number of outcomes.

concepts.title: Building a Model from a Context
concepts.summary: Producing a model means naming the input and output with their units, choosing a family that matches how the data change, and fitting its parameters to the given values.

concepts.title: Reading Parameters and Outputs in Context
concepts.summary: Interpreting a model means stating what each parameter and each predicted output means in the situation, including its units and the interval where it applies.

concepts.title: Assumptions and Limits of a Model
concepts.summary: Every model rests on assumptions such as a constant rate or unlimited growth, and understanding it means knowing which assumption a conclusion depends on.

concepts.title: Judging a Model Against Data
concepts.summary: A model is evaluated by comparing its predictions with observed values, and a pattern in the residuals shows the family is wrong rather than merely imprecise.

concepts.title: Revising a Model
concepts.summary: Improving a model means changing the family, the interval, or the measurements in response to the residual pattern and then re-checking the new predictions.
